situation:
You are the warehouse operations supervisor at STONE RIVER DISTRIBUTION, a regional distributor of grocery and pharmacy goods now in its second year under new leadership after two losing ones. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked you to recommend how the night crew's loading order and bonus should be set for the coming year.

Two contracts signed by the previous leadership now collide. A grocery chain is promised next-morning delivery on every order it places, and a pharmacy wholesaler is promised that its temperature-controlled cases leave the dock first each night. Volume has grown enough that on three nights a week the dock cannot do both.

The night crew is paid a bonus on one figure, the share of orders shipped on time, and the quickest way to raise it is loading grocery pallets first. Loading the pharmacy cases first honors that contract, costs the grocery chain its next-morning windows, and lowers the crew's bonus. Leaving the rule alone protects the bonus and breaks the pharmacy promise on the busiest nights.

The vice president (judge) wants your recommendation on what the night crew should be measured against, and on how you would explain it to them. You will present in the vice president's office. The vice president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the vice president (judge) will thank you for your work.
